extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants and patent examiners in ASEAN Member States (AMS); IP office staff involved in examination, amendment and work-sharing procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on standards for industrial applicability, allowable pre- and post-grant amendments and corrections, support/added‑matter tests, and regional work-product-sharing (ASPEC, PCT‑ASPEC, PPH, validation) applicable to AMS patent practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Industrial applicability — third requirement (contrary to physical laws)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invention fails the third industrial applicability requirement if it operates contrary to well-established physical laws; compliance with clear and complete disclosure (second requirement) is insufficient if the claimed subject-matter cannot be made to work for the special purpose indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical errors not necessarily linked to basic laws of nature may still result in failure to meet the third requirement where they make the claimed subject-matter unusable for the special purpose. Examiner should object where the claimed subject-matter is not usable for the indicated purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date at which requirements must be met (priority date)
rubrics_metrics.description: Verification of compliance with the patentability requirements (e.g., industrial applicability) is carried out as of the priority date of the invention.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Information incorporated into the application after the priority date which was not present in the earlier priority document cannot be relied on to establish industrial applicability as of the priority date and would be considered as adding new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal and response opportunity for industrial applicability objections
rubrics_metrics.description: If an office objects to lack of industrial applicability, the applicant should be allowed to file a response and submit explanation, data or evidence to address the examiner's objections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Whether post-filing data/evidence is admitted depends on the case; usually, if support can be found in the original disclosure the examiner may consider the submitted material. If examiner upholds rejection, appeal to an administrative body or court is available.

rubrics_metrics.name: General rule on amendments (no added technical subject-matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: Amendments are normal but must not add technical subject-matter; full disclosure including optional features and alternative combinations should be provided at filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All AMS allow pre-grant amendments; some allow post-grant. Correction of obvious mistakes is allowed pre- and post-grant. An amendment that adds matter not disclosed in the application as originally filed is not allowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formal and substantive allowability of amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Pre- and post-grant amendments must be formally and substantially allowable: they must not add subject-matter beyond that disclosed in the original application and must not introduce other deficiencies (e.g., lack of clarity or unity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practices as to what constitutes added matter are consistent across AMS patent offices. Examiners should ensure amended applications satisfy filing requirements and other guideline matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural requirements for pre-grant amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may voluntarily amend before filing search/examination request or may amend in response to examiner's written opinion; amendments require prescribed requests, documents, fees and must be filed within prescribed periods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant fails to comply with procedural requirements, Registrar may refuse the request/response. Apart from responding to examiner's opinion, no other opportunity to voluntarily amend exists between filing of the search request and payment of grant fee.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pre-grant amendment effectivity date
rubrics_metrics.description: A pre-grant amendment, once accepted, takes effect from the date the amendment was filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowable amendments test — two conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment is acceptable only if (1) it does not introduce additional subject-matter, and (2) it does not extend the provisional protection conferred by the patent application (except Singapore where post-grant restrictions differ).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These conditions may be verified by applying a novelty test: no new subject-matter must be generated by the amendment. Alteration or excision as well as addition may introduce new subject-matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner's view of acceptable amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: Acceptable amendments include restriction of claim scope; amendments that improve clarity of the description; and desirable claim amendments that do not change subject-matter or scope.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An amended application must satisfy all other filing requirements. Examiners should consider whether claim amendments raise issues of unity, inconsistency with description, or lack of support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special considerations when claims are amended
rubrics_metrics.description: When claims are amended, the examiner must specially consider: (i) unity of invention of amended claims; (ii) whether the description requires corresponding amendment to remove serious inconsistency; (iii) whether all amended claims are supported by the description.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If claim categories are altered, examiner may draw attention to necessary changes in title and/or abstract.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of additional subject-matter (PSIA test)
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment introduces subject-matter extending beyond the application as filed if the overall change causes the Person Skilled in the Art (PSIA) to be presented with information not expressly or inherently presented in the original application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inherency requires that the missing matter is necessarily present and would be recognized by the PSIA; probabilities or possibilities do not establish inherency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Example — added ingredient objection (illustration of added matter)
rubrics_metrics.description: If an application relating to a rubber composition lists several ingredients and the applicant seeks to introduce that a further ingredient may be added, that amendment is normally objected to as new matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments are permitted only within limits of what PSIA would derive directly and unambiguously from the original disclosure using common general knowledge.

rubrics_metrics.name: Range and combination derivability (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: In some cases (e.g., general and preferred ranges disclosed), combinations of disclosed narrower and part-ranges may be derivable from the original disclosure; but care is needed and depends on what a PSIA would directly and unambiguously derive.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess using examples and existing national/regional case law referenced (e.g., EPO Guidelines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Adding specific embodiments (resilient supports example)
rubrics_metrics.description: Introducing a specific feature (e.g., helical springs) not disclosed in the application is normally beyond the disclosure unless it can be shown convincingly that PSIA would regard it as an obvious clarification or drawings/interpretation clearly show the feature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If PSIA would naturally use such a specific embodiment or drawings indicate it, specific reference may be permissible; otherwise objectionable as added matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarification of an effect (technical effect clarification)
rubrics_metrics.description: If a technical feature was disclosed but its effect was not mentioned or fully mentioned, subsequent clarification of that effect may be allowed if it can be deduced without difficulty by a PSIA from the application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Careful assessment required to ensure no new teaching is introduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introduction of further examples or statements of advantage
rubrics_metrics.description: Adding later-filed examples or statements of advantage may extend disclosure and are prima facie suspect, though they may be taken into account by the examiner as evidence supporting allowability (e.g., inventive step) even if not allowed into the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When later examples/evidence are used to support a positive conclusion (e.g., inventive step), mention should be made in the examination report.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments revising the stated technical problem
rubrics_metrics.description: Revising the stated problem to emphasise an effect of a restricted invention is permissible only if the emphasised effect is deducible by a PSIA without difficulty from the application as filed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Revision to emphasise an effect not deducible from the original disclosure is not permissible as it may introduce new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alteration or excision may introduce new subject-matter
rubrics_metrics.description: Changing or removing text (not only adding) may result in a change to the content such that the PSIA would be presented with new information; such alterations must be carefully assessed for added matter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples illustrate that altering example ingredients or layers may produce a panel quite different from the original disclosure and thus be unallowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Missing parts/drawings filed after filing date — reliance on priority document
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicant may file missing drawings or parts of the description subsequently and rely on the priority document to avoid re-dating provided the missing parts were filed within prescribed periods and were 'completely contained' in the priority document.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such missing parts should be considered part of the application documents 'as originally filed' when conditions are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Citation of prior art added after filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally there is no objection to introducing, by amendment, further information regarding prior art which is relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, if the amendment changes the way a PSIA would understand the invention or changes the nature of the problem to be solved, it may be unallowable. Inclusion of prior art that shows advantages is allowable only if such advantage would have been apparent to a PSIA in possession of that prior art.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data/evidence submitted after the filing date (admissibility test)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants may submit data or evidence after filing to address examiner objections; whether admitted depends on field and case but if support exists in original disclosure the examiner may consider it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the data/evidence provides a new teaching (e.g., a selection invention unsupported in the original filing), it is inadmissible. For example, claiming a specific compound by merely providing its advantages later is not allowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarifications removing lack of clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Removal of a lack of clarity will normally not be objected to, provided the change does not extend beyond the disclosure of the application as originally filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trade marks — careful amendment required
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment clarifies the meaning of a trade mark or replaces a registered trade mark with a technical term, the examiner must ensure the amendment does not add subject-matter not disclosed originally.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The composition of a trade-marked product may have changed over time; examiner should be cautious when allowing amendments involving trade marks.

rubrics_metrics.name: International (PCT) applications — original documents constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: For international applications, the documents as originally filed in the PCT phase are the reference; amendments made during PCT or before national entry must not add subject-matter beyond those documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Copies of WO publications can be obtained from the International Bureau; amended/substitute/rectified sheets attached to WO publication must be carefully considered if maintained in national phase.

rubrics_metrics.name: Divisional applications — no extension beyond parent
rubrics_metrics.description: A divisional application's subject-matter may not extend beyond the content of the parent application as originally filed; amendments to divisional after filing may not extend beyond the divisional as filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadening claims — pre-grant vs post-grant rule
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no pre-grant restriction on broadening claims provided the amendment does not add matter beyond the disclosure as filed; post-grant amendments are further restricted — the scope of claims cannot be broadened post-grant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If disclosure is broader than claims as filed, pre-grant amendments may bring claims in line with the specification. Post-grant broadening is disallowed in most AMS.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of support — support between description and claims
rubrics_metrics.description: If subject-matter is disclosed in a claim but not mentioned in the description, it is permissible to amend the description to include that subject-matter, but must ensure the amended description provides required support for the claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contradictions/inconsistencies between claims and description must be resolved by amending either. Each claim limitation must be explicitly or inherently supported in the original disclosure. Negative limitations, exclusions or disclaimers must be examined for potential new matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of proof for amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant has the initial burden of establishing that the requirements for amendment have been met, even if portions of the application supporting the amendments are cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-grant amendments — effect and tests
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-grant amendments, once allowed, take effect and are deemed always to have had effect from the date of grant; the test for added subject-matter is the same as for pre-grant amendments, but scope of claims cannot be broadened post-grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Amendments versus corrections — rectification of obvious mistakes
rubrics_metrics.description: All AMS allow rectification of obvious mistakes pre- and post-grant where the mistake is 'obvious' to the competent authority and the PSIA: (i) something else was intended than what appears; and (ii) nothing else could have been intended than the proposed rectification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The two-fold test: recognition that a mistake was made; and that the proposed rectification was the only meaning that could have been intended. Rectifiable mistakes include linguistic, spelling and grammatical errors so long as meaning would not change. Priority documents should not be taken into account when considering obvious mistakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectification of formula errors and evidence requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Mistakes in chemical or mathematical formulae are generally not rectifiable unless the correct formula is common knowledge; applicant may need to provide evidence to address threshold questions for rectification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For a correction to the description/claims/drawings, the finding by the competent authority must be based only on those documents. Correction, once accepted, takes effect from the date of filing as if the error had never been made.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correction effect — subject-matter addition not relevant
rubrics_metrics.description: Once a change is established to be a correction (rectification of an obvious mistake), the question of whether subject-matter is added or protection extended is not a relevant consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Correction takes effect from filing date; in absence of clear contrary evidence, examiner should assume translations and amendments are accurate but applicant may request correction for obvious errors in translations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Work-product-sharing purpose and scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Work-product-sharing (search & examination results) among patent offices is used to assist offices to conduct S&E more effectively and efficiently, reducing duplication and speeding patent granting for applicants.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work sharing is facilitated via regional (ASPEC), PCT-ASPEC, bilateral, PPH and validation programmes. Use of S&E reports from another office can serve as useful reference when producing quality reports, but recipient offices retain autonomy to decide whether to grant a patent under their national laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASPEC programme — purpose and non‑binding nature
rubrics_metrics.description: ASPEC shares S&E results among nine participating AMS to allow applicants to obtain corresponding patents faster; participating offices may consider but are not obliged to follow findings from other offices.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ASPEC has enabled high allowance rates (reported ~95% for ASPEC-based examination as of Jan 2022). Since 15 June 2021 applicants can use a written opinion establishing at least one allowable claim to request ASPEC before a second AMS office without needing a final S&E report (except Thailand).

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT‑ASPEC eligibility and caps
rubrics_metrics.description: PCT‑ASPEC allows applicants to use a PCT search and examination report prepared by an ASEAN ISA/IPEA to expedite national phase examination in participating AMS; the pilot has an annual cap (100 applications region-wide).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use of PCT S&E report by ASEAN ISA/IPEA; procedures and caps (100/yr) apply; applicants must follow applicable form and procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASPEC AIM — Industry 4.0 acceleration criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: ASPEC AIM accelerates Industry 4.0 Infrastructure and Manufacturing related applications, limited to 50 applications per year with a committed turnaround time of six months for first office action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Eligibility requires that the first IP Office indicates the application contains at least one IPC code qualifying for ASPEC‑AIM acceleration.

rubrics_metrics.name: PPH, bilateral programmes and validation — interoperability
rubrics_metrics.description: Bilateral and national PPH programmes can be paired with ASPEC programmes to further expedite examination; validation and recognition schemes (e.g., Singapore→Cambodia/Lao PDR; EPO→Cambodia) allow simplified filing/validation under specific eligibility conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each programme has its own eligibility and procedural requirements (caps, fees, translations, timing) and may complement ASPEC/RP arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition/validation eligibility (Singapore→Cambodia/Lao; EPO→Cambodia)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognition/validation schemes require conditions such as: applicant first granted patent in Singapore; Singaporean patent in force at filing; filing date on or after specified date (e.g., 11 Feb 2003); for EP→Cambodia, EP application filed on/after 1 Mar 2018 and validation request within three months of EPO grant with Khmer translation of title, abstract and claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures are generally simple and inexpensive but include country-specific timing, translation and fee requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reinforced Partnership (RP) with EPO — reuse of EPO work products
rubrics_metrics.description: RP is an 'office-driven' scheme for standardised reuse of EPO search and examination results to enable partner offices to systematically reuse EPO work products in national/regional grant processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although RP does not require legislative amendments, closer alignment of national laws with the EPC increases benefits; RP can run in parallel with PPH programmes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Obligation to provide available work results from priority applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Some AMS (e.g., Malaysia, Thailand) require applicants to submit information about available work results in relation to priority applications known to the applicant; depending on national law, such information must be furnished automatically or upon request.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is considered a best practice to assist second filing offices in identifying relevant prior art while preserving office autonomy to grant patents.

rubrics_metrics.name: ASPEC request eligibility and correspondence requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify for ASPEC, a patent application filed at a 'second' AMS office must be a corresponding application of the 'first' AMS office and the ASPEC Request must be supported by that first office's S&E documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All claims filed in subsequent patent offices must correspond sufficiently to allowable/patentable claims referred to in the first IP Office's S&E documents. ASEAN Comparative Study Report (CSR) is recommended to assess compatibility of practices across AMS.

rubrics_metrics.name: PCT‑ASPEC and ASPEC AIM specific eligibility requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: PCT‑ASPEC: the basis for examination relied upon must be an international preliminary examination report or a written opinion issued by an ASEAN ISA/IPEA as the first IP Office. ASPEC AIM: the first IP Office must indicate at least one IPC code qualifies for ASPEC‑AIM.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must follow programme-specific forms (e.g., ASPEC Form) and caps/fee rules where applicable.
